I assumed PostgreSQL and a `users` table with an `id` primary key. Tell me if you're on something else (MySQL, SQLite, or an ORM like Alembic or Django) and I'll adapt it.

The migration is split into two files (expand, then contract), so the destructive drop isn't tied to the backfill.

**`001_split_full_name_expand.sql`**

```sql
-- Expand phase: add new columns and backfill. Safe to re-run.
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- Dynamic SQL so this still parses after full_name has been dropped.
DO $migration$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
      AND table_name   = 'users'
      AND column_name  = 'full_name'
  ) THEN
    EXECUTE $sql$
      UPDATE users u
      SET first_name = substring(t.n from '^\S+'),
          last_name  = NULLIF(substring(t.n from '^\S+\s+(.*)$'), '')
      FROM (
        SELECT id, btrim(full_name) AS n
        FROM users
        WHERE full_name IS NOT NULL
          AND btrim(full_name) <> ''
          AND first_name IS NULL      -- only rows not yet migrated
          AND last_name  IS NULL      -- never overwrite manual edits
      ) t
      WHERE u.id = t.id
    $sql$;
  END IF;
END
$migration$;

COMMIT;
```

**`002_split_full_name_contract.sql`** (run only after the app reads and writes the new columns)

```sql
BEGIN;

DO $migration$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
      AND table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'full_name'
  ) THEN
    -- Refuse to drop if any row still has a name that wasn't backfilled.
    IF EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM users
      WHERE btrim(coalesce(full_name, '')) <> '' AND first_name IS NULL
    ) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Unmigrated rows remain; aborting drop of full_name';
    END IF;
    ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN full_name;
  END IF;
END
$migration$;

COMMIT;
```

**Optional rollback** (`001_down.sql`)

```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS full_name text;
UPDATE users
SET full_name = btrim(concat_ws(' ', first_name, last_name))
WHERE full_name IS NULL AND first_name IS NOT NULL;
COMMIT;
-- Drop first_name/last_name manually once you're sure.
```

**Why it's re-runnable**
- `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` makes the schema change a no-op on repeat runs.
- The backfill only touches rows where both new columns are `NULL`, so a second run changes nothing and won't overwrite later edits.
- The `information_schema` check lets the script run harmlessly after `full_name` is gone.
- Everything runs in one transaction, so a failure leaves nothing half-applied.

**Caveats**
- The split is naive: the first whitespace-delimited token becomes `first_name` and the rest becomes `last_name`. "Mary Ann Smith" gives `Mary` / `Ann Smith`, and single-word names get a `NULL` last name. Names with multi-word first names or particles ("van der Berg") will need manual review or a different rule.
- On a very large table, the single `UPDATE` holds locks and generates lots of WAL. In that case, batch the backfill (e.g. `WHERE id BETWEEN ...` ranges, committed per batch). The same guards keep it re-runnable.
- Between the two migrations, new writes to `full_name` won't populate the new columns unless the app (or a trigger) dual-writes. Re-running `001` picks up those rows, since they still have `NULL` new columns.

I can also write this as an Alembic or Django migration, or add the batched backfill, if you'd like.
